candidates.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
candidates.description: No difference in nucleus accumbens (NAcc) response during gain anticipation between fibromyalgia patients and healthy controls
candidates.citation_sentence: Compared to healthy controls, patients demonstrated reduced MPFC responses during the anticipation of reward gains, but enhanced MPFC responses in response to non-punishment outcomes. NAcc responses during the anticipation of reward gains, however, did not significantly differ between patients vs. controls (Martucci et al., 2018).
candidates.notes: The original reported a null NAcc finding; the replication also found no group difference, and the authors explicitly state the result is 'consistent with previous findings.' Per the null-claim rule, agreement with the original null claim is classified as success.

candidates.original_title: Altered prefrontal correlates of monetary anticipation and outcome in chronic pain
candidates.description: Martucci et al. (2018) reported that greater medial prefrontal cortex response to non-punishment outcomes was associated with greater mood disturbance.
candidates.citation_sentence: These analyses suggested that across both studies, MPFC response to non-punishment outcome was positively correlated with individual differences in mood disturbance (i.e., greater MPFC response was related to higher mood disturbance as indicated by higher self-reported POMS scores).
candidates.notes: The replication reproduced the positive association, although the within-group association was primarily driven by the fibromyalgia group.
